messages:
deploy-bot: Safety interlock triggered on release v3.4.1 -> error-rate spike on /embeddings (p95 errors 4.8% > auto-rollback 3.0%)
deploy-bot: Suggested action: auto-rollback to v3.4.0 (reason: regression in quantized kernel).
alisa: Seeing the alert, thanks. Can we hold auto-rollback for 15m? we need quick triage to confirm noisy telemetry. :eyes:
mike: +1. Do we have recent eval traces for that route? could be a traffic skew.
sana: Pulling sample traces now. If it's model quality (not infra) we should avoid churn & pin failing version, then manual revert once we confirm.
jordan: Ops concern: if error keeps climbing we might lose customer SLAs. What's current trend?
oncall-bot: p95 errors: 3.9% (5m ago), 4.3% (2m ago), 4.8% (now). Request rate stable.
alisa: OK — plan: 1) Stall auto-rollback (human override) 2) Pin v3.4.0 as fallback on routing 3) Notify customers if >30m 4) Triage traces + heap of failing requests. Agree?
mike: Agreed. How do we stall? who can flip the interlock?
alisa: I can flip it. Command: `deployctl safety interlock override --release=3.4.1 --reason="triage hold" --expires=15m`
sana: Doing sample log grep: `grep "decode_failed" /var/log/embeds/2026-03-18/*.log | head` — a subset shows quantization mismatch in nvidia kernel, severity medium.
jordan: If kernel mismatch, might be a model/compile pairing issue. We should route a small slice to v3.4.0 and monitor before full rollback.
mike: Can we pin traffic at router level? prefer graceful split: 80/20 -> 50/50 -> rollback if errors persist.
oncall-bot: routing API: `redwood route update --service=embeddings --split=80:20 --versions=3.4.1,3.4.0`
alisa: I'll do 80/20 to v3.4.0 now. I'll also post a short customer note draft in #customer-success for review.
sana: Copy that — I'll keep digging on kernel/quant mismatch. If traces show consistent model-side diffs, we should do full manual revert.
mike: Heads-up for release notes: we may need to label v3.4.1 as "reverted due to quantization regression" and include guidance for dedicated customers.
jordan: Who will own the rollback comms if we go manual? alisa?
alisa: I'll own comms. @sana please be ready to assemble the technical postmortem if we revert.
oncall-bot: safety interlock status: OVERRIDE ENABLED by alisa until +900s.
deploy-bot: Routing update applied: embeddings service set to 80% v3.4.1, 20% v3.4.0.
sana: Initial sample set: 20 failures, 18 contain `quant_dequant_mismatch` stack — looks reproducible.
mike: Recommend we prepare manual rollback runbook steps now. I pasted the checklist below:
```
- announce in #eng-releases and #incidents
- pin release in control plane
- scale up v3.4.0 pool by +2 GPUs
- route 100% to v3.4.0 during low-traffic window (or asap if errors >5%)
- monitor p95, error-rate, and tail latency for 30m
- publish rollback note + incident ticket
```

jordan: I will spin the extra GPUs on standby. ETA 6m.
alisa: If errors cross 5% in next 10m, we escalate to immediate 100% cutover. Otherwise we'll wait for post-triage decision at +15m.
oncall-bot: p95 errors now 5.1% -> threshold crossed.
mike: That crosses our SLA trigger. Proceed with immediate 100% manual rollback.
alisa: Executing rollback runbook now. Pinning fallback & routing 100% to v3.4.0. Command: `redwood release pin --service=embeddings --version=3.4.0 --note="manual rollback due to quantization regression"`
deploy-bot: Routing update applied: embeddings service now 100% v3.4.0.
oncall-bot: Monitoring: p95 errors dropping -> 1.1% (2m), 0.9% (5m)
sana: Confirmed: error signature disappeared after cutover. Will start collecting artifacts for postmortem.
mike: Great. alisa please file incident ticket and publish short customer blurb. I'll draft the technical rollback note.
jordan: GPU scale-down in progress.
alisa: Filing incident INC-2026-2345 and posting customer blurb to #customer-success for review. Quick blurb: "We rolled back embeddings to v3.4.0 due to a regression in the 3.4.1 quantized build impacting a subset of requests. No data loss. We’re investigating and will follow up with a technical report"
sana: Adding triage notes + sample traces to the incident.
mike: Thanks team — we should also add a pre-deploy smoke for quantized kernels to avoid recurrence. I'll open a ticket. :thumbsup:
alisa: Closing thread when incident is filed. Good coordination. :white_check_mark:
